policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'he calleth his own sheep by name' renders either verb identically; φωνεῖ and καλεῖ are both 'calleth' in English and no note is mapped here.

The variant is a bare connective καί. ASV opens 'When he hath put forth' with no 'And', but an unrendered sentence-initial connective is not evidence that the Greek lacked it; the English does not distinguish.
ASV reads 'all his own' — the quantifier πάντα. r01's noun πρόβατα would give 'his own sheep', which the ASV does not read here.
Future indicative and aorist subjunctive after οὐ μή are both rendered 'will they not follow'; the ASV wording cannot distinguish the two forms.

ASV 'what things they were which he spake' backshifts the indirect question regardless of whether the Greek stands in the imperfect indicative or the present subjunctive; the only note on the verse is classed alternative_rendering ('Or, proverb') and does not touch this unit.
ASV renders the dative pronoun: 'Jesus therefore said unto them again.'
Recitative ὅτι before direct speech ('I am the door of the sheep') is not rendered in English either way; its presence or absence leaves no trace in the ASV.
ASV prints 'All that came before me' in the text, and its note — classed textual_variant — reads 'Some ancient authorities omit before me,' putting r01's omission in the margin.
The variant is the connective δέ alone. ASV opens 'He that is a hireling' with no adversative, but an unrendered δέ does not settle whether the Greek carried it.
ASV 'whose own the sheep are not' reads 'are' whether the Greek verb is singular with a neuter plural subject or plural; number of the Greek copula is invisible in the English.
ASV reads 'and scattereth them' — a pronoun object. r01's added noun phrase τὰ πρόβατα would give 'scattereth the sheep', which the ASV does not read.

ASV reads 'he fleeth because he is a hireling' — a pronoun subject with no adversative. r01's clause Ὁ δὲ μισθωτὸς φεύγει would give 'But the hireling fleeth', repeating the noun, which the ASV does not read.
ASV 'and mine own know me' is active with 'mine own' as subject; r01's passive γινώσκομαι ὑπὸ τῶν ἐμῶν would give 'and I am known of mine own.'
The variant is only the order of δεῖ and με; 'them also I must bring' renders either. Both notes on the verse are classed alternative_rendering and decide no reading.

ASV's text reads the plural 'they shall become one flock', matching plural γενήσονται; the singular 'there shall be one flock' is offered only in a note classed alternative_rendering, which cannot decide a reading.
The variant is only the order of με and ὁ πατήρ; 'Therefore doth the Father love me' renders either order.
ASV's text has the present 'No one taketh it away from me', and its note classed textual_variant — 'Some ancient authorities read took it away' — assigns the aorist ἦρεν to the margin.
The variant is the connective οὖν alone; 'There arose a division again among the Jews' supplies no inferential word, but an unrendered οὖν does not settle the Greek.
The variant is the connective δέ alone; 'Others said' renders ἄλλοι with or without it.
Aorist ἀνοῖξαι and present ἀνοίγειν infinitives after δύναται are both 'open' in 'Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?'

ASV's text reads 'And it was the feast of the dedication', rendering the connective δέ, while its note classed textual_variant — 'Some ancient authorities read At that time was the feast' — places τότε in the margin.
The variant is the article with Ἱεροσολύμοις; 'at Jerusalem' renders the place name identically with or without it.
The variant is a bare connective καί before χειμών; the ASV's clause 'it was winter' shows no conjunction, but an unrendered connective does not settle the Greek.
The variant is the article before Σολομῶνος; the English possessive 'Solomon's porch' renders the name the same way with or without it.
ASV subordinates the clause — 'because ye are not of my sheep' — rendering ὅτι; r01's coordinating γάρ would give 'for ye are not of my sheep.'
ASV ends the verse at 'of my sheep' with nothing answering r01's added clause καθὼς εἶπον ὑμῖν, 'as I said unto you.'
ASV 'My sheep hear my voice' uses an English plural whether the Greek verb is plural or singular with the neuter plural subject τὰ πρόβατα.
The variant is only the order of δίδωμι αὐτοῖς and ζωὴν αἰώνιον; 'and I give unto them eternal life' renders either.

ASV's text reads the masculine relative — 'My Father, who hath given them unto me' — and its note classed textual_variant, 'Some ancient authorities read That which my Father hath given unto me,' assigns the neuter ὅ to the margin.

English requires an object with 'hath given ... unto me' whether or not αὐτά stands in the Greek, and the ASV does not mark 'them' as a supply; the wording therefore does not distinguish the readings.

ASV's subject is the personal 'My Father, who ...', so the predicate is masculine and r01's neuter μεῖζόν (which belongs with the neuter relative the ASV puts in the margin) is excluded; r00-base and r02 differ only in the order of πάντων and μείζων, which 'is greater than all' does not distinguish.
ASV reads 'out of the Father's hand' with no possessive; r01's added μου would give 'my Father's hand.'
The variant is the connective οὖν alone; 'The Jews took up stones again' supplies no inferential word, but an unrendered οὖν does not settle the Greek.
All three readings contain the same words and differ only in order; 'Many good works have I showed you' renders any of them.
ASV reads 'from the Father' with no possessive; r01's added μου would give 'from my Father.'
The variant is the order and form of the pronoun with λιθάζετε; 'do ye stone me' renders either, and the ASV marks no emphasis on 'me'.
ASV reads 'The Jews answered him, For a good work ...' with nothing answering r01's added participle λέγοντες, 'saying.'
Recitative ὅτι before the quotation 'I said, Ye are gods' leaves no trace in English; the ASV cannot distinguish its presence from its absence.
Present and aorist imperatives are both 'believe the works' in English; the ASV wording does not distinguish the aspect.
ASV reads 'that ye may know and understand', rendering γινώσκητε; r01's πιστεύσητε would give 'and believe.'
ASV reads 'and I in the Father', naming the noun; r01's αὐτῷ would give 'and I in him.'
The variant is only the order of πάλιν and αὐτόν; 'They sought again to take him' renders either.
Both readings contain the same words and differ only in order; 'And many believed on him there' renders either.
